title: Probe CUDA/Tensor-Core execution for Boolean Fourfold relation composition
hypothesis: For sufficiently large or dense Boolean relation blocks, an aligned FP16/BF16 CUDA GEMM may reproduce exact Boolean support faster than the stdlib CSR oracle once inputs remain resident on an NVIDIA GPU. One-shot transfer, dense packing and result canonicalization may erase that advantage for sparse or small Fourfold workloads.

hardware_boundary.target: CUDA matrix multiplication submitted through PyTorch/cuBLAS
hardware_boundary.tensor_cores: candidate only when device capability, dtype and selected cuBLAS kernel permit; external profiling is required to prove actual Tensor-Core use
hardware_boundary.rt_cores: not used; ray traversal/intersection hardware is not a general semiring executor
hardware_boundary.raster_units: not used; graphics rasterization is not the selected computational contract
hardware_boundary.natural_semiring: not admitted because FP16/BF16 path multiplicities are not exact in general
hardware_boundary.evidence_semiring: not admitted; provenance remains on the CPU/reference boundary

experiment_contract.input: two exact Boolean TypedRelationBlock values with one shared typed middle axis and one exact Fourfold subject
experiment_contract.encoding: canonical CSR support is scattered into zero-padded FP16/BF16 dense matrices aligned to 8- or 16-element tiles
experiment_contract.operation: torch.matmul on CUDA followed by support > 0
experiment_contract.correctness: when the bounded CPU oracle executes, every retained row/column support entry must be exactly equal
measurements: CUDA kernel median/min/max with explicit synchronization
device-to-host support readback and canonical TypedRelationBlock reconstruction
resident-kernel and one-shot ratios against the CPU oracle
reported_environment: dtype, tile multiple, padded size, density and exact reference operation count

bounds.additional_vram_rule: the estimate must also fit inside half of currently free device memory

verification.cpu_contracts: success; includes lazy optional-torch import, strict bounds, deterministic typed fixture, exact CPU Boolean matmul contract, non-authorizing blocked report and atomic strict-JSON output
verification.repository_collection: success; collection-only, not a full-suite execution claim
verification.gpu_execution: not executed by GitHub-hosted CPU runners and not claimed

owner_reproduction.prerequisite: a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build matching the installed NVIDIA driver
owner_reproduction.interpretation: compare cpu_over_resident_gpu_kernel with cpu_over_gpu_one_shot; a large resident ratio without a one-shot crossover means GPU residency or batching is required, not that the product path is faster

kill_or_redesign: Boolean support differs from the exact stdlib CSR oracle
dense packing or readback dominates realistic Fourfold workloads
VRAM expansion is unacceptable at observed graph sparsity
no repeated-query break-even exists against preindexed Forest/relation dictionaries
the result depends on more information or a different query than the baseline
a simpler CPU bitset or Rust sparse kernel yields the same benefit with lower complexity
next_if_positive: Retain matrices on-device across a frozen query batch, benchmark against BM25 plus relation dictionaries and a Rust CPU bitset baseline, then consider one removable Rust/CUDA adapter that remains observationally equal to the reference kernel.
